## Natural history notes

A small moth fly characterized by its delicate, fuzzy body, broad hairy wings held roof-like over the back, and long antennae that give it a tiny gnat-like appearance. In Florida, it is found in moist habitats such as wetlands, swamps, marsh edges, damp forests, drainage areas, and other places with decaying organic matter or wet substrates. Adults are weak fliers and often rest on vegetation or shaded surfaces, while the larvae develop in moist organic material, helping break down decaying plant matter and contributing to nutrient cycling in wet habitats.
